answer: The dawn multiplier is published, charged in sparrow, and island lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 18 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2067 identities would post 521 proofs and burn roughly 69 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
